    All Classes and Interfaces

    Class
    Description
    AnnotatedElements
    The elements a Step gets in a round, by annotation, and by meta-annotation for the step's meta-annotations; and the root elements of the round, if the step processes them.
    Annotation
    An annotation to write, such as @Override or @SuppressWarnings({"unchecked", "rawtypes"}).
    Annotation.Builder
    A builder of Annotations.
    AnnotationReader
    Reads the values of an annotation, defaults included, with the types they are declared with.
    ApplicationDirectories
    The directories where one application stores its files: its own subdirectories of the platform's Directories, one for each kind of file, never shared with another kind.
    ArrayTypeName
    The name of an array type, such as String[].
    Ascii
    Classes, case mapping, comparison and trimming of ASCII characters, as many protocols, file formats and identifiers define them.
    AtomicFiles
    Writes files atomically: a reader sees either the previous content of a file or its new content, never a part of it, and so does the next run of a program after a crash.
    AtomicFiles.Output
    Writes the content of a file to a stream.
    BigFraction
    An exact fraction of two BigInteger values, always in lowest terms and with a positive denominator.
    ByteReader
    Reads a stream of bytes: numbers in either byte order, runs of bytes, text and lines, with lookahead and search.
    Bytes
    An immutable sequence of bytes, usable as a value: two instances with the same bytes are equal, and instances are ordered by their bytes.
    Bytes.Content
    Writes bytes to a writer, for Bytes.build(Content).
    ByteSink
    A writable destination of bytes, such as a file, that opens a new writer each time it is written.
    ByteSource
    A readable source of bytes, such as a file or a URL, that opens a new reader each time it is read.
    ByteWriter
    Writes a stream of bytes: numbers in either byte order, runs of bytes and text.
    Chances<T>
    The exact chances of each outcome of something random: of each element that a RandomSelector selects, or of each multiset that a RandomTable draws.
    CharReader
    Reads a stream of characters: lines, runs of characters, lookahead and search, for reading text formats.
    Charsets
    Charsets that gaia relies on.
    CharSink
    A writable destination of characters, such as a text file, that opens a new writer each time it is written.
    CharSource
    A readable source of characters, such as a text file or a string, that opens a new reader each time it is read.
    CharWriter
    Writes a stream of characters, with calls that chain.
    ClassName
    The name of a class, interface, enum, record or annotation type, possibly nested in others.
    CodeBlock
    A fragment of code: statements, an expression, or Javadoc text, with placeholders for the types and names it refers to.
    CodeBlock.Builder
    A builder of CodeBlocks.
    Compilation
    The outcome of a TestCompiler run: whether it succeeded, every diagnostic, and every generated file.
    CompilationAssert
    AssertJ assertions on a Compilation.
    CompilationExtension
    Gives tests the Elements and Types of a running compilation, to test code that works on javax.lang.model without writing an annotation processor around it.
    Configuration
    How a memory file system behaves: its path style, roots, working directory, capacity, name matching, attribute views, default attributes, clock and features.
    Configuration.Builder
    A builder of Configurations.
    DiagnosticAssert
    AssertJ assertions on the diagnostics of a Compilation that matched an earlier assertion, such as CompilationAssert.hadErrorContaining(String).
    Diagnostics
    Reports errors, warnings and notes at a precise place in the source: an element, one of its annotations, or one attribute of that annotation.
    DiceChances
    The exact chances of each outcome of a DiceExpression: the value it evaluates to, together with the tags that apply.
    DiceChances.Outcome
    One way for an expression to turn out.
    DiceExpression
    A dice expression, such as 4d6dl1 or (1d20:critical>=20:miss=1)+STR+BONUS>=AC: a tree of DiceNodes that is parsed from a text, inspected, rolled, and whose chances are computed exactly.
    DiceNode<T>
    One node of a DiceExpression, whose children are of type T.
    DiceNode.Arithmetic<T>
    An arithmetic operation on two values, such as 1d8+3.
    DiceNode.Bound<T>
    A variable that was given a value.
    DiceNode.Comparison<T>
    A comparison of two values, such as 1d20+5>=AC, which evaluates to 1 if it holds and to 0 if not.
    DiceNode.Condition<T>
    One condition of a DiceNode.Tag: the value of the group, compared to an operand.
    DiceNode.Constant<T>
    A whole number, such as 20.
    DiceNode.Dice<T>
    Dice that are rolled and summed, such as 4d6dl1, 2d8r<=2x or 4d[-1..1].
    DiceNode.Explode
    Which dice explode, that is, add another die that may explode too: DiceNode.Explode.NONE, those that show their DiceNode.Explode.HIGHEST face, or those whose face satisfies a condition.
    DiceNode.Explode.Faces
    Whether dice explode, and on which faces.
    DiceNode.Group<T>
    A value between parentheses, with the tags it's given, such as (1d20:critical>=20:miss=1).
    DiceNode.Keep
    Which of the rolled dice count in the sum: DiceNode.Keep.ALL of them, or the highest or the lowest ones.
    DiceNode.Keep.Mode
    Whether dice are kept or dropped, and from which end.
    DiceNode.Negate<T>
    The opposite of a value, such as -STR.
    DiceNode.Operator
    An arithmetic operation.
    DiceNode.Relation
    How two values are compared.
    DiceNode.Reroll
    Which dice are rolled again: DiceNode.Reroll.NONE, those that show their lowest face, or those whose face satisfies a condition, either once or until the face no longer does.
    DiceNode.Reroll.Target
    On which faces dice are rerolled.
    DiceNode.Reroll.Times
    Whether dice are rerolled, and how many times.
    DiceNode.Sides<T>
    The faces of a die: numbered from one to a number of sides, or listed one by one.
    DiceNode.Sides.Custom<T>
    Faces listed one by one, in ascending order, such as the [-1..1] of 4d[-1..1] or the [0,0,0,0,1,1] of a die that counts a success two times out of six.
    DiceNode.Sides.Standard<T>
    Faces numbered from one to a number of sides, such as the 6 of 3d6.
    DiceNode.Tag<T>
    A tag on a DiceNode.Group, such as :critical>=20 or :tier2>=12<=16.
    DiceNode.Variable<T>
    A variable that has no value yet, such as STR.
    DiceParseException
    Thrown when a text isn't a dice expression.
    Directories
    The base directories where applications store their files, as defined by the XDG Base Directory Specification.
    Environment
    A source of environment variables: the running JVM's, or fixed ones for tests.
    EventBus
    Delivers each event it is given to the subscribers of the event's class and of all its supertypes.
    EventBus.Builder
    Builds an EventBus.
    FakeDirectories
    Directories under one root directory, such as a test's temporary directory, so that code under test never touches the real ones.
    FakeDirectories.Builder
    Builds FakeDirectories.
    FakePlatform
    A Platform with the operating system of your choice and its directories under a root directory, such as a test's temporary directory.
    FakePlatform.Builder
    Builds a FakePlatform.
    FakeRandom
    A RandomGenerator that gives the numbers a test scripted, in order, so that tests of code that uses randomness are exact.
    FakeTicker
    A Ticker that only moves when told to, so that tests of timing code are exact and instant.
    Feature
    An optional capability of a file system.
    Field
    A field, such as private static final int LIMIT = 10;.
    Field.Builder
    A builder of Fields.
    Fraction
    An exact fraction, always in lowest terms and with a positive denominator: an IntFraction, a LongFraction or a BigFraction, which differ by the size of their terms.
    GeneratedSources
    Writes the Java source files a processor generates, with their package declaration and imports: modelled as a JavaFile, or written as text.
    HashListMultimap<K,V>
    A modifiable list multimap backed by a HashMap from each key to a ArrayList of its values.
    HashMultiset<E>
    A modifiable multiset backed by a HashMap, the multiset counterpart of HashSet.
    HashSetMultimap<K,V>
    A modifiable set multimap backed by a HashMap from each key to a HashSet of its values.
    IntFraction
    An exact fraction of two int values, always in lowest terms and with a positive denominator.
    IntIntConsumer
    An operation on an int key and its int value, such as an entry of an IntIntMap.
    IntIntMap
    A hash map from int keys to int values, which stores both without boxing them.
    IntIntPredicate
    A condition on an int key and its int value, such as an entry of an IntIntMap.
    IntMath
    Arithmetic on int values that Math doesn't provide: divisors, powers, logarithms, square roots and divisions with a rounding mode, saturated arithmetic, combinatorics and primality.
    JavaFile
    A Java source file: a package, one top-level type, and the imports they need, which are worked out when the file is written.
    JavaFile.Builder
    A builder of JavaFiles.
    ListMultimap<K,V>
    A multimap that keeps the values of each key in a list, in the order they were added, duplicates included.
    LongFraction
    An exact fraction of two long values, always in lowest terms and with a positive denominator.
    LongMath
    Arithmetic on long values that Math doesn't provide: divisors, powers, logarithms, square roots and divisions with a rounding mode, saturated arithmetic, combinatorics and primality.
    Maps
    Static factories and collectors for unmodifiable maps that iterate in the order their keys are given.
    MemoryFileSystems
    Creates file systems in memory.
    Method
    A method, a constructor, or the compact constructor of a record.
    Method.Builder
    A builder of Methods.
    MoreCollectors
    Collectors that Collectors does not provide.
    MoreElements
    Navigation, casts and checks on Elements that javax.lang.model does not provide.
    MoreGatherers
    Gatherers that Gatherers does not provide.
    MoreGatherers.IndexedFunction<T,R>
    A function of an element and its index in a stream.
    MoreGatherers.IndexedPredicate<T>
    A predicate of an element and its index in a stream.
    MoreTypes
    Checks and conversions on TypeMirrors that javax.lang.model does not provide.
    Multimap<K,V>
    A collection that maps keys to values, like a Map, but where a key may have several values: its entries are key-value pairs, and a key is in the multimap as long as it has a value.
    MultimapAssert<K,V>
    AssertJ assertions on a Multimap.
    Multimaps
    Static factories and collectors for unmodifiable multimaps that iterate over their keys in the order they first appear, and over the values of a key in the order they are given.
    Multiset<E>
    A collection that counts how many times it contains each element: its occurrences.
    Multiset.Entry<E>
    An element of a multiset with its count.
    MultisetAssert<E>
    AssertJ assertions on a Multiset: the assertions on any collection, such as contains or hasSize, which counts occurrences, and assertions on the count of each element.
    Multisets
    Static factories and a collector for unmodifiable multisets that iterate in the order their elements first appear, with all occurrences of an element in a row: multiset("foo", "bar", "foo") iterates over foo, foo, bar.
    MutableRandomSelector<T>
    A weighted RandomSelector whose elements and weights change: an element is added, removed or given another weight, and selected, in a time that grows with the logarithm of the number of elements.
    NameAllocator
    Hands out Java identifiers that do not clash: each new name is the suggestion, made a valid identifier, with as many underscores appended as needed to differ from the keywords and the names already handed out.
    NameMatching
    How the names of the files of a directory are matched when they are looked up.
    NamingConvention
    A naming convention: a way to write a name made of several words, such as timeoutSeconds or timeout-seconds, and the conversion from one to another.
    OnVirtualThread
    Subscribes a method as @Subscribe does, but has each of its events delivered on a new virtual thread, with VirtualThreadExecutor.
    OperatingSystem
    The operating systems a Platform can tell apart: one for each of Platform.isLinux(), Platform.isMacOS() and Platform.isWindows(), and one for the other Unix-like systems, for which all three are false.
    Parameter
    A parameter of a method or constructor, or a component of a record, such as final String name.
    Parameter.Builder
    A builder of Parameters.
    ParameterizedTypeName
    The name of a parameterized type, such as Map<String, List<Integer>>, or of an inner class whose enclosing type has type arguments or annotations, such as Outer<String>.Inner.
    PathStyle
    How the paths of a file system are written: their separators, roots and the characters their names may have.
    Platform
    The platform the JVM runs on: its operating system and the directories applications use on it.
    Platform.Builder
    Detects a Platform from its sources.
    PlatformPreset
    The system properties and environment variables a JVM typically has on an operating system, to detect a Platform from, so that tests run the real detection of the directories of any operating system:
    PlatformPreset.Builder
    Builds a PlatformPreset.
    Preconditions
    Checks that a method is called correctly, and throws the matching exception if not.
    PrimitiveTypeName
    The name of a primitive type, or void.
    ProcessingContext
    Everything a processor works with: javac's processing environment, and gaia's helpers on top of it.
    ProcessingException
    An error in the source, thrown to stop processing an element and report the error at a precise place: the element, one of its annotations, or one attribute of that annotation, as Diagnostics reports it.
    ProcessorAssert
    AssertJ assertions on an annotation processor class.
    ProcessorOption<T>
    An option of an annotation processor, given to javac as -Aname=value, with its type and default value.
    RandomBag<T>
    A bag to draw elements from at random, without putting them back: a deck of cards, or a list of options that must each come up once before any comes up again.
    RandomPermutation
    The numbers from zero to a size, in a random order.
    RandomSamples
    Samples: several different elements taken at random among other ones, without taking any twice.
    RandomSelector<T>
    Selects an element at random, each time it's asked to, with the source of randomness it's given.
    RandomSelectorAssert<T>
    AssertJ assertions on how often a RandomSelector selects each element: the selector is asked for many elements, and the counts are compared with what the expected chances make likely.
    RandomStrings
    Random strings: identifiers, tokens and codes made of characters taken at random in an alphabet.
    RandomTable<T>
    A table to draw from at random: each draw gives a multiset of elements, made of the entries that are always given and of entries selected by weight, each of which is an element in some quantity, another table, or nothing.
    RandomTable.Builder<T>
    Builds a RandomTable.
    Range<C>
    An interval of comparable values: all the values between a lower and an upper bound.
    Range.Bound<C>
    A bound of a range: closed, open, or absent.
    Range.Bound.Closed<C>
    A bound that includes its endpoint.
    Range.Bound.Open<C>
    A bound that excludes its endpoint.
    Range.Bound.Unbounded<C>
    The absence of a bound: the range extends forever on that side.
    RangeAssert<C>
    AssertJ assertions on a Range.
    RecordingRandom
    A RandomGenerator that gives the numbers of another one and remembers them, to play them again with a FakeRandom: a behavior that came up once with real randomness becomes a test that always has it.
    RolledExpression
    What a DiceExpression evaluated to: a tree of RolledNodes with the same shape as the expression, in which each node has a value, each die a face, and each tag applies or not.
    RolledNode<T>
    One node of a RolledExpression, whose children are of type T: a DiceNode together with what it evaluated to.
    RolledNode.Arithmetic<T>
    An arithmetic operation on two values.
    RolledNode.Bound<T>
    A variable and the value it was given.
    RolledNode.Comparison<T>
    A comparison of two values.
    RolledNode.Constant<T>
    A whole number.
    RolledNode.Dice<T>
    Dice that were rolled.
    RolledNode.Die
    One die that was rolled.
    RolledNode.Group<T>
    A value between parentheses, with its tags.
    RolledNode.Negate<T>
    The opposite of a value.
    RolledNode.Tag<T>
    A tag on a RolledNode.Group, and whether it applies to this roll.
    Seed
    A seed from which other seeds are derived by name or by number, so that each part of a program has a random sequence of its own that only depends on the seed and on what the part is, not on what was generated before it.
    ServiceFiles
    Writes the service files ServiceLoader reads on the class path: META-INF/services/<service>, listing the implementations of a service, one binary name per line.
    SetMultimap<K,V>
    A multimap that keeps the values of each key in a set, without duplicates: adding an entry it already contains leaves it unchanged.
    Sets
    Static factories and a collector for unmodifiable sets that iterate in the order their elements are given.
    SharedCompilation
    Makes CompilationExtension share one compilation across all the tests of the annotated class, and its nested classes, instead of starting one per test.
    SortedMultiset<E>
    A multiset that keeps its elements sorted, by their natural ordering or by a comparator: the multiset counterpart of NavigableSet.
    SourceScope
    The names a generated source file uses, and the imports they need: a GeneratedSources.write(JavaFile, Element...) body gets one to name the types it refers to.
    Splitter
    Splits text into parts around a separator: a character, a literal string or a regular expression.
    Step
    One unit of work of a StepProcessor: the processing of the elements annotated with some annotations, or with annotations that some meta-annotations annotate, and optionally of every root element.
    StepProcessor
    An annotation processor made of Steps, which takes care of processing rounds.
    Stopwatch
    Measures elapsed time, on a Ticker rather than on the wall clock.
    Subscribe
    Marks a method that receives events once its listener is registered: the events of the type of its parameter, and of the subtypes of that type.
    SubscriberIndex
    Subscribes the @Subscribe methods a class declares, and those with a subscribing annotation: implemented by the code gaia-processor generates for that class, and found by EventBus.register(Object) with ServiceLoader.
    SubscriberIndex.Registrar
    Subscribes the methods of a listener, on behalf of the event bus.
    SubscribingAnnotation
    Marks an annotation that subscribes the methods it annotates as @Subscribe does, and has the bus deliver their events through an executor, such as on a given thread.
    Subscription
    What EventBus.subscribe(Class, java.util.function.Consumer) or EventBus.register(Object) subscribed, until it is closed.
    SystemProperties
    A source of system properties: the running JVM's, or fixed ones for tests.
    TestCompiler
    Compiles in-memory sources with the system Java compiler, in process, running the given annotation processors.
    Text
    Finds text in a string, to extract, remove or replace it.
    Text.Affix
    A literal string that a text starts or ends with: a prefix or a suffix.
    Text.Pattern
    Selects at most one occurrence in a text, to extract, remove or replace it.
    Throwables
    Creates exceptions from the exception that caused them.
    Ticker
    A source of nanosecond time, for measuring elapsed time: only the difference between two readings is meaningful.
    TreeMultiset<E>
    A modifiable sorted multiset backed by a TreeMap, the multiset counterpart of TreeSet.
    Type
    A class, interface, enum, record or annotation type, or an anonymous class.
    Type.Builder
    A builder of Types.
    Type.Kind
    The kinds of type.
    TypeKey
    A TypeMirror with the equals and hashCode of the type it denotes, for use in sets and maps: TypeMirror itself does not define them, and two mirrors of List<String> need not be equal.
    TypeName
    The name of a type as it is written in source code: a primitive, a class, a parameterized type, an array, a type variable or a wildcard, possibly with type annotations such as @Nullable.
    TypeVariableName
    The name of a type variable, such as T.
    UnresolvedVariableException
    Thrown when a dice expression is rolled, or its chances computed, while some of its variables have no value.
    Version
    A version number as Semantic Versioning 2.0.0 defines it, such as 1.4.0-rc.1+build.5: a major, minor and patch version, then optional pre-release identifiers after -, then optional build metadata identifiers after +.
    VirtualThreadExecutor
    Runs each task on a new virtual thread: the executor of @OnVirtualThread.
    Visibility
    How widely an element can be accessed, as its access modifier, or the lack of one, says: see MoreElements.visibility(javax.lang.model.element.Element) and MoreElements.effectiveVisibility(javax.lang.model.element.Element).
    WildcardTypeName
    The name of a wildcard type argument: ?, ? extends T or ? super T.
